design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 01 « Parcours bout-en-bout » steps 1→3 (Accueil → modale « Nouveau livre » → Arbre initial avec Sommaire + Mort déjà présents) = the BINDING visual target for the creation flow. Component anatomy + tokens come from the design system (styles.css): the dialog is a `surfaces/Modal` over a scrim, the title input is a `forms/Field`, « Créer » is the accent primary button. Low-fi wireframe fidelity, light theme only.

plan.goal: Let an author create a new book — name it, seed its initial tree (Sommaire + an isolated « Mort du personnage »), and land in the editor — as the entry point of the whole authoring flow.

design_contract._binding: Reproduce the wireframe creation modal using design-system components only; where prose and the DS disagree, the DS tokens win. No new px values — reuse Modal/Field/Card anatomy.
design_contract.dialog: Centered `surfaces/Modal` (radius var(--r-3xl), 1px var(--border-card), var(--shadow-modal)) over a flat ink scrim (no blur). Header « Nouveau livre » (--fs-row/600). Body = one `forms/Field` labelled « TITRE » (mono var(--fs-eyebrow), uppercase, var(--track-eyebrow)) with a text input (var(--surface-sunken), 1px var(--border-field), var(--r-md)) carrying a placeholder (e.g. « La Caverne d'Aldûr »); a blinking accent caret is acceptable. Footer = right-aligned « Annuler » (ghost: 1px var(--border-field)) + « Créer » (accent: bg var(--accent), text var(--accent-fg), --fw-semibold). No destructive slot.
design_contract.trigger: Home screen « + Nouveau livre » affordance = the dashed accent card from the wireframe (1.5px dashed var(--accent), var(--accent) « + », var(--r-md)). Owned here for the walking skeleton; later hosted by book-library.
design_contract.seeded_tree: Immediately after create, the editor canvas shows exactly two nodes (wireframe § 01 step 3): a `NodeBadge kind='sommaire'` node at the top (entry/root, empty text zone showing an inviting placeholder « Écrivez ici le texte d'introduction… ») and an isolated `NodeBadge kind='mort'` node bottom-right (gray-hatch, zero edges). No other nodes, no edges.

acceptance_criteria: From the home screen, a « + Nouveau livre » affordance opens a creation dialog containing a single « Titre » field plus « Annuler » and « Créer » actions.
« Créer » is disabled while the trimmed title is empty; pressing Enter in the field is equivalent to « Créer »; the field is focused when the dialog opens.
On « Créer », BookService persists a new book whose tree contains EXACTLY two seeded nodes — one `sommaire` node (empty text zone, the entry/root) and one `mort` node — and zero other nodes.
The seeded « Mort du personnage » node is isolated: zero incoming and zero outgoing edges, flagged as the obligatory failure leaf; it is never auto-linked on creation.
After a successful create the app navigates to the new book's editor (canvas view) with that book opened, and emits `book:created` then `book:opened` (in that order) carrying the new bookId.

Every created book receives a unique, collision-free id and a created_at timestamp; the id (not the title) is the persistence key, so duplicate titles are allowed; the title is stored trimmed and verbatim.
« Annuler », Esc, or scrim click closes the dialog with no book created and no events emitted; focus returns to the triggering affordance.

A created book is immediately retrievable via BookService.listBooks()/getBook(id) and survives reload (persisted via PersistenceService); when offline the create is queued through CloudSyncService and does not block navigation.
The dialog renders strictly from design-system tokens/components (Modal, Field, accent primary), light theme; ≥44px hit targets on « Créer »/« Annuler ».

Empty elements invite action: the « Titre » input shows a placeholder (e.g. « La Caverne d'Aldûr »), and the seeded Sommaire's empty text zone shows an inviting placeholder prompting the author to write the introduction (project-wide empty-state rule).
plan.walking_skeleton: A « + Nouveau livre » button opens a minimal dialog (single title field + « Créer »). On submit, call BookService.createBook(title) — which seeds the Sommaire + isolated Mort nodes and persists — then emit book:created → book:opened and navigate to the editor route for the new bookId. No validation polish, no animation, no offline queue yet: just the end-to-end create → seed → navigate slice wired through brain. Depends on a minimal BookService (the API nœud) existing in brain; if absent, stand up the smallest createBook/getBook/listBooks that seeds and persists, to be hardened by the BookService owner later.

iterations.goal: Dialog UX & validation: focus the field on open; « Créer » disabled until the trimmed title is non-empty (computed inline, no useEffect derived state, KR-013); Enter submits; Annuler/Esc/scrim dismiss with focus restored to the trigger; trim on submit. Full design-system fidelity pass (Modal/Field/accent primary, light theme).

Seed contract & events: route creation through a single BookService.createBook factory that atomically seeds exactly the Sommaire + isolated Mort nodes with a collision-free id + created_at; emit book:created → book:opened in order AFTER persistence resolves; navigate only on success. Add tests asserting node count = 2, Mort edge count = 0, and event order.

Persistence & cloud-first: persist the new book under its persistenceKeys.ts key (no raw localStorage in the feature, KR-011); restore on reload; queue the create via CloudSyncService when offline without blocking navigation; never lose a create on a failed network call. Regression test for the offline-create path.

known_risks: KR-001 — Seed must be atomic and EXACT: a book must always contain exactly the Sommaire + isolated Mort nodes. A partial seed (only one node, or Mort accidentally wired) silently corrupts every downstream feature (tree-canvas, game-preview). Seed through one BookService factory, never ad hoc in the feature.
KR-002 — The « Mort du personnage » node is isolated by contract (0 edges) and obligatory; never auto-link it on create. Relinking is the author's explicit act, owned by choice-linking.

KR-003 — Book id must be collision-free and stable; the id, not the title, is the persistence key. Titles may duplicate. Generate ids via brain/utils (no Math.random collisions, no title-derived slugs).

KR-004 — Navigation and events must fire only AFTER persistence resolves, in the order book:created → book:opened, so listeners (library refresh, editor mount) observe a persisted book. Out-of-order emission races the editor mount.

KR-005 — Cloud-first: the local write is the source of truth when offline; the create must be queued for sync via CloudSyncService and must not block navigation. Never drop a create on a failed network call.
KR-011 — No raw window.localStorage in feature files; persist only through PersistenceService/persistenceKeys.ts (global config KR-111).
KR-013 — Do not use useEffect for the « can create » derived state; compute it inline from the trimmed title (global config KR-113), and avoid exhaustive-deps disables.

A11y — the dialog is a focus trap: focus the field on open, support Esc/scrim dismiss, and restore focus to the triggering affordance on close; « Créer »/« Annuler » keyboard-accessible with ≥44px targets.

Dependency — book-creation consumes BookService (brain). If BookService is not yet built, the walking skeleton stands up a minimal createBook/getBook/listBooks that the BookService owner later hardens; do not fork a second seeding path (re-asserts KR-001).

resolved_decisions: Sommaire is seeded as an EMPTY text zone that shows an inviting placeholder (not pre-filled text) — per the project-wide empty-state rule.
No character/hero seeding here: the editor and the play (book-launch) mode are distinct; the hero is created when a reader launches the book, out of this feature's scope.
Creation captures the title only — no cover image or extra metadata for now.

The seeded « Mort du personnage » node is LOCKED for the book's life: not deletable, not duplicable, type fixed; only its text is editable. It is the single death leaf (reached on trap failure or lost combat).
